source_neutral.procedure: Examine the physical sheets, envelopes and wrappers of the undated correspondence bundle for previously undetected material traces of manufacture, writing, posting, receipt and storage. Record the found arrangement and keep it distinct from original order. Document each item, establish handling and exposure limits, apply non-contact imaging in increasing exposure order, record reproducible localized responses and non-responses, and translate supported findings into date intervals, groupings and pairwise relations. Compare these constraints with handwriting, event mentions, custody records and available dated comparison material. Whether the items are originals rather than copies is unverified; their period and paper type are unknown, as are the existence of detectable traces and the availability of securely dated items in or near the bundle.
source_neutral.action: Before probing, record the found order, assign folio numbers or references without marking the items, and photograph each under visible light to provide the reference for judging whether a later response was previously absent. Agree an exposure and handling ceiling with a conservator, checking whether probing could compromise planned ink or paper sampling or analysis. If so, perform that sampling or analysis first or withhold probing for the affected items. Select probes according to the suspected trace's capacity to produce a response and apply them in increasing exposure order: transmitted light for watermarks and mould structure; raking light from several directions for indentations and blind embossing; ultraviolet-induced fluorescence and, if available, infrared imaging for faded ink, erased pencil and abraded postmarks. Use no chemical reagents, moistening or contact methods. Apply the same sequence to every item and to securely dated items from the same creator or custody, if available, to compare responses and non-responses. Where feasible, have the person capturing and logging responses work without knowledge of the sequence hypothesized from textual clues. For each signal, record item reference, position, probe, settings and legibility. Record non-responses by item and probe with the same care, and record comparison-item responses alongside them so that signal types can be assessed against material of known date.
source_neutral.observables: A response qualifies as a signal only when it is localized on the sheet, absent from the initial visible-light photograph and reproduced in a second capture. Candidate manufacture traces include watermarks, countermarks, chain- and laid-line patterns and blind-embossed stationer's stamps. Transmitted light may reveal a watermark design, initials or date figure and chain-line spacing. Raking light may reveal indented line shapes, whether or not legible as text, and blind embossing. Fluorescing or absorbing patterns may have the shape of faded or abraded postmarks, faded or erased dockets, endorsements or annotations. Storage-contact signals may include mirror-image ink offset, shared stains, fastener rust marks or fold shadows; an offset, stain or rust outline may correspond in shape to a feature on another item. Non-responses, changes in item condition and whether repeat capture produces any new localized response are also recorded or monitored.
source_neutral.inferential_warrant: A signal initially supports only the presence, at its recorded location, of material capable of producing that response. A watermark or stamp supports identification of paper stock. A dated or independently datable mould supports an earliest possible date for the paper's manufacture. Shared stock supports grouping items without ordering them. Indentations on item A that are legible as item B's text support that B was written while lying over A's sheet and support a relative link between their writing events; the direction A written after B is argued only if A's ink can be seen to run across the indentations. A recovered postmark or docket legible as a date supports a posting or receipt date for its bearing object. It supplies an absolute date constraint for a letter only when the object's association with that letter is independently supported. Matching offset, stain or rust outlines support past physical contact, bearing on storage arrangement and possibly recovery of an earlier order, without establishing writing order. Enter each inferred constraint as an interval or pairwise relation alongside handwriting, event mentions and custody records. Agreement among independent clues narrows an interval; retain conflicts as alternative chronologies. Check every constraint derived from a previously undetected trace against at least one independent dated reference or another reference document before using it to fix a date.
source_neutral.problem_decomposition: The physical units are individual sheets, envelopes and wrappers, each identified and located within the recorded found arrangement. Their relevant events are manufacture, writing, posting, receipt and storage, whose dates and relations are assessed separately. Manufacture traces connect items to paper stocks and potentially to dated moulds; common stock defines groups. Indentations connect a sheet beneath another sheet to the writing performed above it, with an additional ink-crossing condition for the specified direction between writing events. Postmarks and dockets connect dates to their bearing objects, while independently supported object-to-letter associations are required to transfer those date constraints to letters. Offset, stains, rust and fold shadows concern physical contact and storage relationships. Securely dated comparison items from the same creator or custody provide response comparisons. Intervals and pairwise relations are combined with independent documentary clues while preserving alternative chronologies where constraints conflict.
source_neutral.next_inquiry: Before any constraint derived from a previously undetected material trace is used to fix a date, check it against at least one independent dated reference or another reference document.
source_neutral.limits: Similar responses can arise from unrelated causes: fluorescence may result from later repair adhesives, sizing, mould, foxing or annotations by later owners or archivists; indentations may result from later note-taking on top of the bundle; offsets and rust marks may result from later rearrangement or refastening. A watermark design may have been used for many years, and paper may have been stored long before use. Non-response may result from unwatermarked or trimmed sheets, indentations removed by pressing, flattening or humidification, or ink or pencil faded or cleaned below detection. It therefore does not establish that an item is unrelated, differently dated or never posted. Paper date does not establish writing date, writing date does not establish posting date, an envelope may not belong to its current letter, and storage contact does not establish composition sequence. Light and ultraviolet exposure and handling have cumulative effects and may alter inks or paper needed for later analysis. Observe the agreed exposure and handling ceiling and the specified sequencing or withholding of probes where later analysis could be compromised. Stop work on an item when its exposure ceiling is reached, any condition change is seen, or repeat capture adds no new localized response. Stop the entire procedure if the conservator withdraws approval. The procedure can support bounded intervals and some pairwise relations. If no independently dated reference survives corroboration, the justified result is restricted to relative or grouped chronology with stated open alternatives, and no absolute dates are asserted. Feasibility depends on unverified access to originals, equipment and conservator approval.
